catalogue_scope: Source-backed, non-chemical management guidance for the six current tomato and potato model labels. Chemical recommendations are intentionally withheld pending current product-label and registration verification.

diagnostic_limitations: A model healthy classification is not proof that the whole plant is disease-free. The model only supports this leaf-image class.
non_chemical_management: No disease medicine is indicated for a healthy classification.
records.applicable_region: India; general guidance, not a location-specific prescription

sources.title: Tomato — KAU Agri-Infotech Portal
sources.supports: Crop rotation and disease-free seed/seedlings are described in the tomato crop guidance; displayed here only as general prevention, not disease treatment.

symptoms: Brown circular leaf lesions that may enlarge and develop concentric rings; a yellow halo and coalescing lesions may occur.
diagnostic_limitations: Visible spots are not sufficient to confirm Alternaria; other pathogens, nutrient problems, chemical injury, and environmental stress can look similar. Image assessment is preliminary.
non_chemical_management: Use disease-free seed from healthy fruit.
Collect and dispose of affected crop debris.
records.applicable_region: India; confirm local advice and current guidance

symptoms: Light-green marginal leaf lesions can darken and coalesce; white growth may appear in wet, humid conditions.
diagnostic_limitations: A photograph cannot establish the pathogen. Late blight can progress rapidly; seek local agricultural advice promptly if suspected.
non_chemical_management: Remove infected debris using locally approved disposal practices.
records.applicable_region: India; confirm local advice and current guidance

sources.title: Potato late blight — KAU Agri-Infotech Portal
sources.supports: KAU recommends disease-free seed potatoes and field sanitation as disease prevention; displayed here only as general prevention.

symptoms: Older lower leaves may develop circular brown spots with dry, papery concentric rings and yellowing; tubers can also show depressed lesions.
diagnostic_limitations: Leaf appearance alone cannot confirm the pathogen or exclude other causes; tuber symptoms are not assessable from a leaf-only image.
non_chemical_management: Collect and dispose of crop debris and potential host plants.
Avoid waterlogging and use fertilizer judiciously.
records.applicable_region: India; confirm local advice and current guidance

sources.title: Potato early blight — KAU e-Crop Doctor
sources.supports: Symptoms and the listed non-chemical management practices.

symptoms: Water-soaked lesions often begin near leaf edges; white growth may occur underneath. Stems and tubers can also be affected.
diagnostic_limitations: A photograph cannot confirm the pathogen. KAU describes rapid disease progression; seek local agricultural advice promptly if suspected.
non_chemical_management: Inspect seed potatoes and remove affected tubers.
Keep tubers covered by adequate ridges.
Remove infected debris and volunteer host plants.
records.applicable_region: India; confirm local advice and current guidance
